finding: The main business object has two live names. The stories, the business process and all three CDMs say resource description (CDM class ResourceDescription). The catalogue-be API says SelfDescription in every schema and path, the adapter uses both (/selfDescriptions for search, /resourceDescriptions for participant and federated detail), and catalogue-client-be uses selfDescriptions. The federated operations still to be defined (F-022, F-052) force a builder to pick one.
evidence: BP05B and BP06 titles and steps: "resource description"; CDM:catalogue-be:ResourceDescription; catalogue-be common-components.yaml schemas SelfDescription, SelfDescriptions, SelfDescriptionResult, SelfDescriptionStatus; catalogue-be paths /self-descriptions and /selfDescriptions/quickSearch; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /selfDescriptions and GET /participants/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}, GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}; catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId}. The catalogue-client-be CDM already removed SelfDescription: "SelfDescription is not a concept of the Federated Catalogue CDM, which owns the resource description as ResourceDescription".
question: Which name do new operations, schemas and events use, and is self-description kept only as a legacy wire name with a written mapping?
options: Resource description in all new contracts and texts; existing SelfDescription schemas and /selfDescriptions paths stay as documented legacy names, mapped in the glossary
Rename the existing schemas and paths to ResourceDescription (breaking change, versioned API)
Keep self-description on the wire everywhere and resource description in business texts, with the mapping written down

finding: A resource description is identified under at least eight names, and it is not stated which of them name the same value. The search result items carry only claimsGraphUri, the detail call takes selfDescriptionId, the adapter takes resourceDescriptionId, and catalogue-be has both a per-record id and a resourceKey "stable across versions". A tester cannot pass the identifier from a search result to the detail call with confidence, and a builder cannot tell whether revoke and QAR act on one version or on the whole resource description.
evidence: CDM:catalogue-be:ResourceDescription.resourceIdentifier; catalogue-be SelfDescription.id, .sdHash, .resourceKey ("Stable identifier for the resource across versions"), path selfDescriptionId, DELETE /self-descriptions/{self_description_hash}, GET /self-descriptions filters ids and hashes; query-mapper-adapter-be path resourceDescriptionId and GET .../version "list of resource descriptions with the same parent resource description id"; search items n.claimsGraphUri (catalogue-be, adapter) and i.claimsGraphUri (catalogue-client-be v1); catalogue-client-be selfDescriptionId example did:web:registry.gaia-x.eu:DataOffering:...; SIMPL-31150, SIMPL-31153, SIMPL-31770 technical descriptions: "resource identifier".
question: Which identifier names a resource description across its versions, which names one version, and is the claimsGraphUri of a search result the selfDescriptionId and resourceDescriptionId of the detail calls?
options: resourceIdentifier (= resourceKey) for the resource description across versions, id for one version; search results expose resourceIdentifier; paths use {resourceDescriptionId}
One identifier only (the credential subject id, today claimsGraphUri); versions addressed by version number
Keep all names, and add a written mapping per API to the CDM identifier

finding: The overall quality result has four names for the score and four for the classification. The criteria filter on overallCategory, which no API or CDM has. The Consumer-facing search (catalogue-client-be v1) returns qualityScore and qualityClassification, while catalogue-be and the adapter return overallScore and overallClassification. A test written from the criteria asserts on a field the response does not carry.
evidence: SIMPL-29292/AC2, SIMPL-29293/AC2: "overallScore"; SIMPL-29292/AC3, SIMPL-29293/AC3: "overallCategory"; SIMPL-27998/AC1: "overall score"; SIMPL-31140 Scenario 4, SIMPL-31143/AC1, SIMPL-31769/AC1, BP6.7.3: "metadata quality score", "quality classification"; catalogue-be SearchResponsePayload n.overallScore, n.overallClassification and SelfDescriptionQualityOverallResult.score, .classification; query-mapper-adapter-be searchResponsePayload n.overallScore, n.overallClassification; catalogue-client-be v1 GET /selfDescriptions example i.qualityScore, i.qualityClassification; CDM:query-mapper-adapter-be:QualityAssessmentRecord.qualityScore and data-quality-rules.md QualityAssessmentRecord.qualityScore, qualityClassification, OverallQualityRating.weightedScore; catalogue-client-be.md: "SelfDescriptionScore".
question: Which field names does a search result and a detail carry for the overall score and classification, and is overallCategory meant as overallClassification?
options: Business terms overall quality score and overall quality classification; wire names overallScore and overallClassification in every API; CDM attributes renamed to match
Wire names qualityScore and qualityClassification as in the CDM and the Consumer-facing API; catalogue-be and adapter renamed
Keep both, with a written mapping per API, and correct the criteria to the Consumer-facing names

finding: "Federated catalogue" names two different things. In the stories and the business process it is a catalogue of another (Trustor) data space. In the CDMs and API texts the Federated Catalogue is the catalogue-be service of the own data space, and the adapter's local search says it searches "the Federated Catalogue". A builder of the federated search can read a requirement on federated catalogues as one on the own catalogue service.
evidence: SIMPL-31102/AC2: "the list of federated catalogues"; SIMPL-31768: "only from the catalogues of federated data spaces"; BP06 search scopes: "Federated catalogue search: search across multiple data spaces"; CDM:query-mapper-adapter-be:FederatedCatalogue ("stores ResourceDescriptions and evaluates catalogue search requests"), CDM:catalogue-client-be:FederatedCatalogue, schema-manager-be.md FederatedCatalogue; catalogue-be.md purpose: "Federated Catalogue Service (simpl-fc-service)"; query-mapper-adapter-be GET /selfDescriptions (local): "Search the Federated Catalogue for Resource descriptions"; federatedResourceDescriptionPayload: "Complete Federated Catalogue resource description"; catalogue-client-be v1 q: "filter self-descriptions in the federated catalog".
question: Which name does the catalogue-be service carry in business texts and CDMs, so that federated catalogue only means a catalogue of a Trustor data space?
options: Federated catalogue only for a Trustor data space's catalogue (as BP06); the service becomes catalogue service (catalogue-be) in CDMs and API texts
Keep Federated Catalogue for the service, and say catalogue of a federated data space (or Trustor catalogue) in stories and APIs
Define both meanings in the glossary and qualify each use

finding: The lifecycle of a resource description is not defined once. The CDM and API know active and revoked; the criteria and the process speak of submitted, valid, published, not published and stored. The process revokes the previous version when a new one is published, but no transition or state covers that. The publish operation can answer 202 "accepted but the validation is not finished yet", a pending state that no value set has. DELETE removes a description "entirely", a step the process does not have.
evidence: CDM:catalogue-be:ResourceDescription.lifecycleStatus: active, revoked; catalogue-be SelfDescriptionStatus enum active, revoked; SIMPL-27998/AC1 to AC3: "published in the catalogue", "not stored"; BP05B.07 "published", BP05B.11 and BP5B.5.10 "revokes the current (previous) resource description version"; catalogue-be POST /self-descriptions 202: "The request was accepted but the validation is not finished yet"; DELETE /self-descriptions/{self_description_hash}; catalogue-be.md: "Deletion removes it entirely from the catalogue"; query-mapper-adapter-be PATCH /participants/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}: revoke, idempotent.
question: Is published the business label of active, is there a pending state after submission, does a superseded version become revoked or a separate state, and is deletion part of the lifecycle?
options: States published (stored value active) and revoked; superseded versions become revoked; no pending state (202 removed); delete is an administrative purge outside the lifecycle
Add states pending and superseded to the CDM value set and the API enum, with the transitions listed next to the CDM
Keep active and revoked as written and change the criteria to say active

finding: "Active" carries three meanings: a lifecycle value of a resource description, the Metadata Quality Profile resolved for the latest published schema version (whose own lifecycle has no active value), and a catalogue's federation flag. The trust relation behind that flag is also called trusted, no longer trusted, federation enabled and authenticated.
evidence: catalogue-be SelfDescriptionStatus active; catalogue-client-be GET /schemas/{schemaName}/qualityProfiles/active: "active Metadata Quality Profile resolved for the latest published schema version"; schema-manager-be.md MetadataQualityProfile.lifecycleStatus: PUBLISHED, REVOKED; catalogue-client-be v1 CatalogueInfo.active and catalogue-client-be.md Catalogue: "whether its federation status is active"; SIMPL-31113/AC2 "no longer consider trusted GA as trusted"; SIMPL-31150/AC1 "its federation with this Governance Authority is still enabled"; SIMPL-31150/AC2 "unauthenticated or no-longer-trusted".
question: Which word names each of the three concepts, and what are the values of the federation (trust) status?
options: Resource description: published; profile: applicable (or active) Metadata Quality Profile, defined in the glossary; catalogue: federation enabled / disabled
Keep active for all three and define each use in the glossary

finding: The parts of a Quality Assessment Record have three sets of names. The owning CDM (Quality Scoring Service) has OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating and RuleOutcome. The catalogue-be API redefines them as SelfDescriptionQualityOverallResult, ...DimensionResult and ...RuleResult with other attribute names, and the Consumer-facing record uses SelfDescriptionScore, DimensionScore and RuleEvaluation. The record is also exposed twice: as an opaque JSON-LD graph and as a structured qualityAssessment in the publication response. The threshold source is called metadata quality definition, Metadata Quality Profile and Minimum Quality Profile.
evidence: data-quality-rules.md: OverallQualityRating.weightedScore, thresholdStatus; DimensionRating.score, dimensionWeight, thresholdStatus; RuleOutcome.outcome, ruleType; catalogue-be SelfDescriptionQualityAssessment {rules, dimensions, overall}, SelfDescriptionQualityRuleResult {id, name, status}, SelfDescriptionQualityStatus PASSED, FAILED; catalogue-be QualityAssessmentRecord {@context, @graph}; SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse.qualityAssessment; catalogue-client-be.md: "SelfDescriptionScore, DimensionScore and RuleEvaluation of the response are OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating and RuleOutcome"; SIMPL-27998/AC1 "metadata quality definition", AC2 "metadata quality definition (MQP)"; SIMPL-29292/AC3 "Metadata Quality Profile (MQP)"; catalogue-client-be v1 GET /selfDescriptions: "active Minimum Quality Profile (MQP)".
question: Does the catalogue API use the owner's names for the record's parts, and which representation is the Quality Assessment Record the catalogue stores and returns?
options: Use the Quality Scoring Service names (OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating, RuleOutcome and their attributes) in every API; the JSON-LD graph is the record, the structured form is a documented projection
Keep the catalogue-be names as the catalogue's own read model, marked as a projection of the external record in the CDM

finding: Resource type and offering type look like one concept with two names and four spellings: lower case (data, application, infrastructure), upper case (DATA, APPLICATION), short forms (App, Infra, Data) and PascalCase shape names (Application, DataOffering). The schema stories reject a SEARCH schema when a resourceType is given, so the accepted values matter for the 400 tests.
evidence: CDM:catalogue-be:GeneralServiceProperties.offeringType: data, infrastructure, application; catalogue-be search example offeringType infrastructure, data; catalogue-client-be v2 GET /schemas example resourceType APPLICATION, DATA, parameter example data; schema-manager-be.md: "resourceType: open value set; PascalCase strings ..., e.g. Application, DataOffering"; SIMPL-31815 hints: "(App, Infra, Data)"; SIMPL-31817/AC2: "a resourceType for instance \"DATA\""; BP05B.01: "resource type (data, application, or infrastructure)"; catalogue-client-be.md OfferingType: "Which representation ... is authoritative is not defined".
question: Are resource type and offering type the same concept, and which values and spelling do the API, the CDM and the criteria use?
options: One concept, resource type, with the closed set data, application, infrastructure in lower case; offeringType kept as the shape's property name and mapped
Two concepts: offering type (closed set on the description) and resource type (open, PascalCase, on the schema), each defined in the glossary

finding: "Schema" names different things in one component. catalogue-be's /schemas operations manage the original catalogue store of ontologies, shapes and vocabularies (OntologySchema, latest composite schema), while its CDM says schema management is external and those legacy endpoints are excluded. The Schema Manager schema has a schemaName, a schemaType and versions. The schema is identified as schemaId, schemaName, name or uri depending on the API. The stories send schema creation to "POST /schemas", which in catalogue-be is the legacy store.

question: Which schema concept do catalogue-be's /schemas operations expose, are they still in scope, and which identifier names a schema?
options: The catalogue references the Schema Manager schema only, identified by schemaName; catalogue-be's legacy /schemas operations are removed from the contract
Keep the legacy store under another name (for example ontology store) and reserve schema for the Schema Manager concept

finding: Identity attributes, their federation mapping and discovery access policies carry the federated search criteria, but no CDM in the input set models them, as owned or as external. The only related class, AccessPolicyFilter, is owned by the Query Mapper, is "interaction only", and never appears in the stories. The same ideas have many names: identity attributes, public identity attributes, Consumer's attributes, mapped attributes, User-Attributes; discovery access policies, access policy values, discovery ABAC.

Keep them out of the catalogue CDMs and state in the CDM that the gateway owns all of it, removing the policy steps from the catalogue criteria

finding: Each API has a CDM, but the alignment tables no longer match the entry files. The catalogue-be CDM says legacy schema and session endpoints are excluded, yet the tier 1 entry file has them, and the generic /query operation has no concept at all. The Query Mapper CDM lists neither the Governance Authority search operations nor the federated detail operation, and its scope does not mention federation. The catalogue-client-be CDM lists /governanceAuthority operations that its v1 file does not have, and places the detail operation with catalogueId in v1 while it is in the v2 entry file.

Keep the operations and add their concepts to the CDMs
